idea.value: The film performs its own promise: a drafting grid and raw chrome tiles are pushed, morph by morph, into a polished interface, so the product's promise, a rough draft turned into finished work, is shown as one continuous transformation rather than claimed.

audience.value: Solo video editors and motion designers who want results that look studio-made; the offer is a subscription to editable project files plus tutorials.
evidence: speech-text.json words 6.72-9.88 (voice names solo editors wanting studio-level results)
speech-text.json screenText 13.51-15.02 (pill labels for tutorials and project files)

value.device: wireframe layout guide: crosshair lines with node dots, words typed into the gap one by one, then the guide frame pulls outward and a metal tile grows out of its centre
value.description: 0.00-1.54 s the frame is a white layout sketch: two horizontal and two vertical hairlines with four node dots, and the first three spoken words land between them, each flashing a tint for two to three frames before settling to black. At 1.58 s the guide box starts expanding past the frame edges, the words part to left and right, and a dot at the centre grows into a chrome tile by 2.00 s. The viewer is shown a sketch becoming an object in the first two seconds, which is the whole film in miniature.

value.purpose: hook: set the premise (every piece starts rough) on a literal sketch
value.retentionDevice: words appear ahead of the voice inside a drafting grid; empty white invites the eye to the centre
value.content: crosshair layout lines, three words typed between the nodes

value.purpose: the raw idea as an object: unfinished material
value.retentionDevice: the tile grows and rounds its corners, a slow change that keeps the eye on the centre
value.content: grey brushed-metal tile on a faint grid, alone in white

value.purpose: problem: most ideas stall at the sketch stage
value.retentionDevice: the tile implodes to a point and bursts into a field of saturated spheres: the first colour in the film
value.content: iridescent spheres crowding the frame edges, a three-word phrase small at centre

value.purpose: the brand arrives as the answer to the problem
value.retentionDevice: the colour collapses inward and vanishes, leaving a quiet embossed ground; the wordmark types on letter by letter
value.content: white embossed maze ground, wordmark typed at centre

value.purpose: proof of product: the brand opens into the library itself
value.retentionDevice: a pill behind the wordmark grows into a full-bleed gradient card, and interface panels fly in from every edge within 0.3 s
value.content: pink-teal gradient card, central button, dark interface panels at the edges

value.purpose: aspiration: name the level of result the audience wants
value.retentionDevice: two words pinned to the extreme left and right edges frame a dotted globe; the eye travels across the whole width
value.content: pastel particle globe inside a thin circle, one word at each edge

value.purpose: restart the transformation: back to raw material for the second pass
value.retentionDevice: callback to the opening tile: same grey object, new grid colour
value.content: grey gradient tile on a pale grid with faint red guide lines

value.purpose: payoff of the transformation: the raw tile becomes a finished, watchable interface
value.retentionDevice: the tile widens, tints blue and turns into a dark landing page whose headline types on
value.content: dark blue website mock-up at about 62% frame width with a small button under it

value.purpose: what you get: two offer items, shown as stacked buttons
value.retentionDevice: hard cut on the next sentence, a spring pop, then the back button rises over the front one
value.content: two stacked rounded buttons, blue in front then grey in front

value.retentionDevice: the only type-only beat: a short centred sentence builds word by word, darkening to bright blue

value.purpose: call to action as an object: the sentence collapses into a button, which grows
value.retentionDevice: the words fade from the left into a small pill; the pill goes pale, then snaps saturated and larger, then grows
value.content: subscribe button growing from 10% to full frame width

value.purpose: sign-off: brand and address, held long enough to read
value.retentionDevice: the button has become the end card; wordmark types on, slides left, and an address pill types on beside it; then 2.3 s of still hold with no voice
value.content: navy-to-sky vertical gradient, white wordmark, white address pill

payoff.value: 11.51-13.51 s: the same grey tile the film opened with becomes a finished dark landing page; the promise 'rough to finished' is completed on screen, on the line about a piece people actually watch.

callToAction.value: Subscribe button (16.22-18.14 s) that grows into the end card; then wordmark and web address held 18.4-22.6 s. The CTA is never a separate card: it is made from the last sentence and becomes the final ground.

whyItWorks: Form is the argument: every scene is made out of the previous one (frame to tile, tile to spheres, wordmark to card, tile to site, sentence to button, button to end card), so the viewer watches rough material being finished and never needs the claim explained.

One idea per spoken sentence, about 1.7 s each (median corrected hold 1.74 s), with 6 of 11 picture changes within 0.25 s of a sentence start against 20% by chance (window chosen after looking, so suggestive, not proof): the picture turns the page when the voice does.
On-screen words run about 0.18 s ahead of the voice (median of 9 word pairs timed on the strips), so reading confirms hearing instead of chasing it.

Almost all of it sits on a white ground with one object at frame centre; the eye never searches. Colour is rationed: the spheres at 3.5 s and the gradient card at 6.7 s are the only saturated full frames before the blue end card.
The CTA is built from the last line and becomes the end card, so the final 4.5 s are brand and address on the colour the film has been heading towards since the website beat.
